paper.title: WholeBodyVLA: Towards Unified Latent VLA for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation Control

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct end-to-end humanoid whole-body VLA study using action-free human video and RL control.

sections_read.purpose: Identify fragmentation between VLA manipulation and locomotion control.
Inspect latent-action pretraining and LMO control.

sections_read.locator: 4.3 How does action-free videos contribute to loco–manipulation?
sections_read.purpose: Verify the contribution of human video.

research_question: Can action-free human video pretrain a unified latent space for humanoid manipulation and locomotion?
contributions: A unified latent action model plus a discrete loco-manipulation-oriented RL controller.

method.summary: Separate manipulation and locomotion latent models are learned from human video, fused in a VLA, and decoded into whole-body motion through a discrete RL policy.
assumptions: Human video contains reusable latent priors despite lacking robot actions.
A low-level whole-body controller can realize discrete latent motion commands.

study_context.sample_or_scale: Multiple real-robot tasks plus simulation ablations; exact deployment counts vary by task.

evaluation.design: WholeBodyVLA is compared with modular, VLA and velocity-policy baselines; latent-model and controller ablations isolate components.

findings.finding: The unified latent model extracted useful priors from action-free video and materially improved downstream task success.
findings.scope: The paper's evaluated humanoid loco-manipulation tasks.
findings.locator: 4.3 How does action-free videos contribute to loco–manipulation?

author_stated.limitation: Long-horizon dexterous tasks, memory, mapping and active perception remain future work.

reader_inferred.boundary: Performance still depends on accurate stance and low-level execution.
reader_inferred.basis: The failure analysis attributes cases to small stance errors during execution.

transfer_boundary: Supports reuse of action-free visual motion priors, but does not establish arbitrary open-world long-horizon autonomy.

design_strengths: Component ablations separate latent pretraining and control.
design_risks: Custom scores complicate comparison across papers.
Training video and task coverage may share semantic structure.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Multiple representative policy families are evaluated on the same task suite.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task success captures end-to-end behavior, while aggregate scores can hide failure modes.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Architecture and deployment details are supplied in appendices.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Limited to one humanoid and the curated task suite.

evidence_cards.claim: Removing the unified latent action model reduced success by 38.7 percentage points, indicating that action-free human video contributed useful priors in the evaluated tasks.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports action-free human video as a pretraining source for whole-body policies.
evidence_cards.summary: The ablation directly compares the full model with removal of unified latent learning.
evidence_cards.locator: 4.3 How does action-free videos contribute to loco–manipulation?
evidence_cards.source_context: As shown in Table 4.2 , the full model improves success rate by 38.7%, indicating that unified latent learning extracts useful priors from action-free human videos and enhances downstream policy learning.

quantitative.comparator: full model versus model without unified latent learning
quantitative.locator: 4.3 How does action-free videos contribute to loco–manipulation?

verification.rationale: The ablation sentence states the magnitude, component and interpretation.
